messages:
anika: Quick question — who is allowed to flip the kill-switch for feature flag `payment_processing_v2` during today’s canary? We're starting a 10% rollback after seeing a spike. Need to know who to contact if we need emergency off.

kev: Oncall + engineering leads can flip. Operationally it's done via the Feature Flags dashboard (https://redwood.internal/flags) or via `rbctl` if UI is down. See runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kill-switches :eyes:

sasha: Adding: please include an audit reason and ticket number when flipping. If you don't include it the toggle will be auto-reverted and you'll get paged. We enforce this via the toggle-service.

oncall: I'm oncall today. I can flip but prefer eng-lead approval for anything affecting payments. If we hit >0.5% error rate or 5xx surge, I'll disable immediately.

kev: infra-bot will create an audit entry automatically if you use `rbctl`. Example:

```
rbctl toggle set payment_processing_v2 off --by=anika --reason="canary error spike / 502s" --ticket=INC-2345
```

infra-bot: AUTO: toggle requested by anika - creating audit entry (id: audit_20240524_009).

anika: Also, what about auto-fallback? Is there a configured fallback route? We want to route to `payment_v1`.

kev: Yes, routing policy already set to fallback to `payment_v1` and to send webhook to ops for every toggle. Confirmed.

sasha: One more — ensure logs are preserved for at least 90 days and artifacts saved to S3 path: s3://redwood-ops/audits/payment/INC-2345

anika: Thanks. I'll coordinate with @sre_lead and file INC-2345. I'll post back when toggled.

oncall: Ty. If you toggle, ping #incidents and call me (pager) so we can watch latency.
